purpose: Assigned values for the 8-bit profile_id field as it appears in TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT for the BLE binding. Profile identifiers are transport-scoped: profile 1 under BLE and profile 1 under IP are unrelated assignments and must never be compared.
why_this_exists: Before this registry, every binding's examples used profile_id = 1 with no definition anywhere. Two implementations could agree on transport_id 3 and still be unable to talk, because one meant connectionless advertising and the other meant connected GATT with a particular MTU assumption.
A convention that fossilises is worse than an absent one: once shipping code assumes profile 1 means whatever it happens to do, the value cannot be defined later without breaking it.

allocation_policy.0x00: Reserved. Never assigned, so an uninitialised field names no profile.

profiles.name: RESERVED
profiles.detail: Permanently reserved. An offer carrying profile_id 0 is malformed.

profiles.name: BLE-X0-GATT-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Connected GATT carriage: one MCL Link frame per write, fragmented per mcl-ble when the frame exceeds the negotiated ATT payload. Fragmentation is exercised at the 23-byte minimum ATT MTU rather than the larger MTU a host may negotiate, because the minimum is the only value every peer must support. Rendezvous beacon in advertising Service Data for the MCL 128-bit service UUID.
profiles.evidence: mcl-ble/evidence/e4-ble-gatt-20260902/ demonstrated this carriage between two machines. That is transport evidence, not a conformance pass: no normative profile exists to conform to.
profiles.promotion_gate: May be proposed for a Standards Action assignment once a second independent implementation has interoperated with it and the parameters below are fixed by specification rather than by the reference implementation.

profiles.name: BLE-X1-CONNECTIONLESS-EXPERIMENTAL
profiles.detail: Connectionless carriage: a Link frame small enough for the 31-byte advertising payload is broadcast without a connection. Suitable for presence and hazard, which have no addressee. No fragmentation, so a frame that does not fit is not sendable under this profile.
profiles.evidence: The same evidence record decoded a 19-byte Tier-0 PRESENCE Link frame from a scan response.

notes: Experimental Use values were chosen deliberately over 1 and 2. These profiles are defined by reference-implementation behaviour rather than by specification, and an Experimental assignment says so in the value itself. Taking a Standards Action value now would freeze exactly the decision this project's governing rule says to defer: freeze only what future implementers must agree on.
A profile_id says nothing about security. A BLE link with a completed pairing is not an authenticated peer; see mcl-core/SECURITY.md.
An implementation receiving an unassigned profile_id MUST NOT guess. It refuses the offer and may continue on its current transport.
